text:
incident-bot: [PAGE] P1 Alert — dedicated pool 'aurora-prod' reporting sustained 100% GPU utilization for tenant aurora-corp (12m). Latency SLO breach detected. Paging @pager-oncall and SRE on-call.

pager-oncall: Ack — I'm here. Notifying SREs Mina/Javier.

mina: On call, joining. Any customer-facing reports?

aurora-support: Yes — we're getting customer errors (502/timeouts) on inference endpoints. Seems concentrated to aurora-corp traffic.

javier: Looking at infra metrics — tenant queue at 24, GPU memory saturated, processes pinned on model redwood/gpt-13b-q4 (quantized). No hardware faults. Likely large burst from a single tenant run.

lisa: Contract check: aurora-corp has emergency burst enabled but requires explicit approval for billing.

account-exec-sam: I'm on a call with their ops team now — they prefer we avoid bursting if possible, but will authorize in an emergency. Please propose mitigations.

ryan: Two pragmatic mitigations: (A) Enable emergency burst to shared pool (+2-4 GPUs) for immediate relief. (B) Apply graceful degradation: throttle tenant concurrency + route to smaller quantized model (6B) — cheaper and lowers mem. Which do we want first?

mina: Let's try non-billing first. Throttle default concurrency to 4 for aurora-corp and monitor. Command: `rbctl tenant throttle aurora-corp --concurrency 4 --grace 30s`

javier: Throttling applied. Watching queue and tail latency.

incident-bot: Action logged: throttle command executed by mina.

aurora-support: Throttle is live but high-priority pipelines still seeing timeouts. They can't drop fidelity on two premium endpoints.

lisa: We can preserve tagged high-priority endpoints on the existing pool while routing non-critical traffic to fallback.

mina: Implementing fallback route for non-priority traffic: `deploy-tool route set aurora-corp --model redwood/gpt-6b-q4 --match "!priority:high"`

javier: Fallback applied. Pinning priority endpoints to current instances now.

aurora-support: After fallback + throttle, error rate dropped from ~34% -> ~8%. Customer reports slight output degradation on non-critical endpoints but core services OK.

account-exec-sam: Customer ops wants a short burst to fully clear the queue and restore baseline quality for all customers. They approved a 2-GPU emergency burst for 20 minutes.

ryan: Enabling burst per approval: `rbctl burst enable --tenant aurora-corp --gpus 2 --duration 20m --reason "prod outage — customer approved"`

incident-bot: Burst enable event recorded. Autoscale changes: +2 GPUs attached to aurora-prod pool for tenant aurora-corp.

javier: New GPUs are up. Utilization dropped to ~75%, queue draining steadily. Latency returning to normal.

mina: Continue monitoring for 15m after burst ends. Add followups: postmortem + cost estimate.

lisa: SRE lead — can you owner postmortem and check autoscale thresholds and tenant isolation rules?

sre-lead: I'll take ownership. Action items: collect timeline, autoscale logs, tenant burst history, and confirm why scheduled customer test ran at peak — possible mis-scheduled job.

aurora-support: For context — the spike was an internal heavy test that accidentally ran at peak traffic. We're updating their scheduler and will send official notice.

account-exec-sam: Logging customer-approved burst and cost acceptance. Please include that in postmortem.

mina: Mitigations summary for incident board INC-2026-1823: 1) Applied tenant throttle, 2) Routed non-critical traffic to 6B fallback, 3) Preserved priority endpoints, 4) Enabled 2-GPU emergency burst (customer approved).

incident-bot: Incident state updated to MITIGATED. Please file postmortem within 48 hours and tag with `customer-impact` and `dedicated-pool`.

aurora-support: Thanks all — errors cleared and customers are seeing restored service. We'll coordinate scheduling changes to prevent recurrence.

mina: Closing thread after postmortem created. Great work team. :thumbsup:
